okta_password_recovery._comment: Lab 41 (Okta Professional 4.4/5.1). Setting names follow the Okta Identity Engine password policy (Admin Console: Security > Authenticators > Password > policies) and its API fields (complexity.minLength, minLowerCase, minUpperCase, minNumber, minSymbol, excludeUsername, dictionary.common.exclude; age.historyCount, minAgeMinutes, maxAgeDays (0 = never expires); lockout.maxAttempts, autoUnlockMinutes (null = admin must unlock)). Recovery methods follow the policy rule's self-service password reset and unlock options as read in 2026. The exact order in which Okta reports several complexity failures is not documented; check_order is this course's teaching order.

concepts.password policy priority: Okta checks password policies from priority 1 downward and applies the first active policy assigned to one of the user's groups; the Default Policy (Everyone) is always last.
concepts.password history: The number of a user's most recent passwords that cannot be chosen again; older passwords drop out of the window and become usable.
concepts.minimum password age: How long a user must keep a new password before changing it again, which stops someone cycling through the history to reuse an old favourite.
concepts.account lockout: After the set number of failed sign-in attempts the user's status becomes Locked out until an admin unlocks it, the user self-unlocks, or the auto-unlock time passes.
concepts.recovery authenticator: An authenticator the password policy allows for self-service reset or unlock, such as email, phone (SMS or voice) or Okta Verify push; the user must have enrolled it.
concepts.self-service unlock: A password policy option that lets a locked-out user unlock their own account after verifying with an allowed recovery authenticator.
concepts.expire password: An admin action that sets the user to Password expired, so they must choose a new password at their next sign-in.
concepts.clear user sessions: An admin action that ends the user's current Okta sessions, signing them out so a stolen session cookie stops working.
